newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair forms new charter unit.
newsitem.headline: Swissair forms new charter unit.

text.p: Swissair AG said it would reorganise its long-haul charter operations by forming a wholly-owned subsidiary, Charter-Leisure AG.
The new company should take over Swissair's two Airbus A310 aircraft in the second half of this year and employ close to 200 people, most of which are cockpit and cabin personnel.

The aircraft, which will be replaced by A330-200 planes in 1998, will appear in Swissair livery, but also carry the name of Balair/CTA, the company previously responsible for all charter operations in the Swissair group.
In 1995 Swissair dissolved Balair/CTA with Crossair AG taking over short-haul charter operations, while Swissair continued to operate the long-haul.
However, Swissair said in a statement that bringing the long-haul operations under the Swissair umbrella did little to improve the economic viability of the charter business.

"Taking a longer-term view of the picture, it appears obvious that a turnaround can only be achieved with an independent operating company that has a market-conforming cost structure," Swissair said, adding:
"Executive management's goal is to bring long-haul charter operations into the black by 1999 at the latest."
The central elements of a new cost structure are an independent staff of cockpit and cabin personnel.
Swissair and pilot association Aeropers have designed a new career model, which substantially reduces cockpit crew costs.
Pilots will be recruited from Swissair's corps and be obligated to serve eight-to-10 years with Charter-Leisure.

At the new company, the rank of captain will be achieved after fewer years of service, but salaries are lower than at Swissair. After serving at Charter-Leisure, pilots have the choice to either remain with the company or return to Swissair.
Discussions with the staff association for cabin personnel are ongoing, Swissair added.
